Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be an
algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. Let $X$ be a smooth
$k$-scheme of finite type that admits a locally closed immersion into some
projective space over $k$ (that is, $X$ is smooth and quasi-projective;
[[def-locally-closed-immersion]]), let $L$ be an invertible
$\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $W\subseteq\Gamma(X,L)$ be a nonzero
finite-dimensional linear system, with $\dim_kW=r+1$, base locus
$\operatorname{Bs}(W)$ and $X^\circ=X\smallsetminus\operatorname{Bs}(W)$
([[def-linear-system-base-locus]]); thus $\mathbf P(W)=\mathbf P^r_k$.

Then there is a nonempty Zariski-open subset $U\subseteq\mathbf P(W)$ such
that for every closed point $[s]\in U$ of the $k$-scheme $\mathbf P(W)$
(equivalently, by
[[thm-classical-varieties-equivalent-integral-separated-finite-type-schemes]],
every classical parameter $[s]$ lying in $U$), and every representative
$0\ne s\in W$, the closed subscheme $Z(s)\cap X^\circ\subseteq X^\circ$ is
smooth over $k$. Thus the property "the member $Z(s)\cap X^\circ$ is smooth
over $k$" holds for general members of $W$ in the sense of
[[def-linear-system-base-locus]], with generalizing open set $U$; the members
are closed subschemes of the open subscheme $X^\circ$, which may be empty, and
$U$ contains classical parameters.

In particular, suppose $X\ne\varnothing$, fix a locally closed immersion
$X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$, let $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ be the hyperplane line
bundle of that immersion, and let $W_h\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$ be
the hyperplane system, the span of the restrictions of the degree-one forms
([[def-linear-system-base-locus]]). Then $\operatorname{Bs}(W_h)=\varnothing$,
and there is a nonempty Zariski-open subset $U\subseteq\mathbf P(W_h)$ such
that for every closed point $[s]\in U$ the scheme-theoretic hyperplane section
$X\times_{\mathbf P^N_k}V_+(F)$ of $X$ — for any degree-one form $F$ with
$F|_X=s$, equivalently the zero scheme $Z(s)$
([[lem-zero-scheme-of-line-bundle-section]]) — is smooth over $k$.

No irreducibility or connectedness of $X$ or of the members is asserted, and
no statement is made about the dimension or the nonemptiness of the members.

Let $X\subseteq\mathbf P_k^N$ be irreducible of dimension $d\ge1$. If $f$ is homogeneous of positive degree and does not vanish identically on $X$, then $X\cap V_+(f)$ is nonempty and every irreducible component has dimension $d-1$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: The universal incidence $\mathcal X=\{(x,H):x\in X\cap H\}\subseteq X\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ is a projective-space bundle of relative dimension $d-1$ over $X$: at each $x$ the hyperplanes containing $x$ are the linear forms vanishing at $x$, a rank-$d$ subbundle of the rank-$(d+1)$ bundle of linear forms, so the fibres are projective spaces of dimension $d-1$. Hence $\mathcal X$ is smooth, irreducible and of dimension $n+d-1$, and the fibre of $g$ at $(y,H)$ is $f^{-1}(y)\cap H$. A nonempty hyperplane cut of a projective variety of dimension $i+1$ has dimension $i$ unless the hyperplane contains a top-dimensional component, in which case its dimension is $i+1$; this is exactly [F4] applied component by component, taking the zero-dimensional components to be either contained in $H$ or disjoint from it.

Partition the universal locus of fibre dimension $i$ into $A_i=\{(y,H):y\in Y_i,\ \dim(f^{-1}(y)\cap H)=i\}$ and $B_i=\{(y,H):y\in Y_{i+1},\ \dim(f^{-1}(y)\cap H)=i\}$; both are constructible by [F1]. For fixed $y\in Y_i$ the fibre of $A_i$ over $y$ consists of the hyperplanes containing at least one of the finitely many top-dimensional components of $f^{-1}(y)$. Such a component spans a projective linear subspace of dimension at least $i$, so the hyperplanes containing it form a projective subspace of the dual of dimension at most $d-i-1$; hence every fibre of $A_i\to Y_i$ has dimension at most $d-i-1$, and [F2] applied to the finitely many components of $\overline{A_i}$ gives $\dim A_i\le\dim Y_i+d-i-1$. The projection $B_i\to Y_{i+1}$ has fibres of dimension at most $d$ because the hyperplane parameter is free, so $\dim B_i\le\dim Y_{i+1}+d$. Subtracting the source dimension $n+d-1$ of $g$ from twice the fibre dimension plus these parameter dimensions gives contributions at most $r(f)-i$ for $A_i$ and at most $r(f)-1$ for $B_i$; for $i=0$ the $A_0$ contribution is $\dim Y_0-n\le0$ because $\dim Y_0\le\dim\overline{f(X)}\le n$ by [F2].

If $r(f)>0$, both bounds in step 2.1 are at most $r(f)-1$, including the separately treated $i=0$ case, so $r(g)\le r(f)-1$. If $r(f)=0$, the bounds are strictly negative for every $i>0$; for $i=0$ the contribution is zero, attained because $r(f)=0$ forces generic fibre dimension zero by [F2], so $g$ is generically finite on its image and has defect zero, while the strict bounds for positive fibre dimension prove smallness.

For the fixed-hyperplane claim, project each of the finitely many locally closed components of the $A_i$ and $B_i$ to $(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$; a component whose image is not dense is absent from a general parameter fibre, and for a component with dense image [F2] bounds its general parameter fibre dimension by its dimension minus $d$. Intersecting the finitely many resulting nonempty parameter opens with the smooth-section open of [F3] gives a nonempty Zariski open; on it the same estimates as step 2.1 hold with $\dim A_i-d$, $\dim B_i-d$ and source dimension $n-1$ for $X_H$, so the identical arithmetic gives the fixed-hyperplane conclusions, and iterating on the successive smooth nonempty sections proves that a positive defect decreases at every nonempty step. Transversality of a prescribed finite algebraic Whitney stratification is the separately supplied condition named in the Statement, not a consequence of ordinary Bertini alone.

Let $k$ be a field, let $n\geq 0$ be finite, put $P=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, and let
$A=P/I$ with a specified finite generating list $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ for the
actual ideal defining the affine scheme. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset
A$, write $L=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $J(\mathfrak m)$ be the $r\times n$ matrix over
$L$ obtained by mapping the formal partial derivatives $\partial f_i/\partial
t_j$ through $P\to A\to L$.

If $k$ is perfect, then $L/k$ is finite separable and
$$
\operatorname{rank}_L J(\mathfrak m)=n-\dim A_{\mathfrak m}
$$
if and only if $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is a regular local ring. For any field $k$,
the same equivalence holds at a $k$-rational point, where $L=k$, without a
perfectness assumption. If $I=I(X)$ for a reduced classical affine algebraic
set $X$ over an algebraically closed field and $\mathfrak m$ corresponds to a
closed point $x$, then, assuming AC,
$$
\dim A_{\mathfrak m}=\dim_xX=\max_{x\in X_i}\dim X_i,
$$
where $X_i$ ranges over the irreducible components through $x$. The finite
generating list need not be minimal, and $I$ need not be radical in the first
two assertions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a perfect field
([[def-perfect-field]]) and let $X$ be a reduced $k$-scheme of finite type over
$k$. Then:

1. the regular locus $X_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in|X|:\mathcal O_{X,x}\text{ is a regular local ring}\}$
   ([[def-singular-and-regular-loci-variety]]) is open in $X$;
2. for every irreducible component $Z$ of $X$
   ([[def-irreducible-component-of-a-topological-space]]) the intersection
   $X_{\mathrm{reg}}\cap Z$ is a dense open subset of $Z$; in particular every
   irreducible component contains a nonempty dense open subset of points
   regular on $X$;
3. if $X\ne\varnothing$, then $X_{\mathrm{reg}}\ne\varnothing$.

No separatedness, irreducibility or equidimensionality hypothesis is imposed,
and $X$ may be empty, in which case the second clause is vacuous and the third
is not asserted.

Let $m,n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^m\times\mathbb C^n$ be open, let
$f:U\to\mathbb C^n$ be holomorphic, and let $(a,b)\in U$ satisfy $f(a,b)=0$.
Assume the complex Jacobian with respect to the second block is invertible:

$$\det\left(\frac{\partial f_j}{\partial w_k}(a,b)\right)_{1\le j,k\le n}\ne0.$$

Then there are neighbourhoods $A$ of $a$ and $B$ of $b$, and a unique
holomorphic map $\varphi:A\to B$, such that

$$f(z,\varphi(z))=0\qquad(z\in A),$$

and, after shrinking $A\times B$ if needed,

$$f(z,w)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w=\varphi(z).$$

Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, regarded as a
classical variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) with its
analytic topology, its smooth points (regular local rings) and its finite
smooth algebraic frontier stratifications
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]).

(a) **Whitney conditions.** Let $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ be a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification whose strata are pure-dimensional, and let $R\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ be incident strata. In local analytic charts of an ambient smooth manifold, the pair $(S,R)$ satisfies **Whitney (a)** at $y\in R$ if for every sequence $x_n\in S$ with $x_n\to y$ whose tangent planes $T_{x_n}S$ converge to a plane $T$, one has $T_yR\subseteq T$; it satisfies **Whitney (b)** at $y$ if additionally, whenever $y_n\in R$ with $y_n\to y$ and the real secant lines through $x_n,y_n$ converge to a line $\ell$, one has $\ell\subseteq T$. A **finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification** of $X$ is a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification satisfying (a) and (b) at every point of every incident pair. Coordinate independence of the limits and the implication (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), commonly used in the literature, are not assumed as proved here; requiring both conditions makes the intended interface explicit.

(b) **Tube control data.** A system of **tube control data** on the analytic stratified space $X$ consists of an open neighbourhood $T_R$ of each stratum $R$, a continuous retraction $\pi_R:T_R\to R$ and a continuous radius $\rho_R:T_R\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\rho_R^{-1}(0)=R$, both maps are smooth on each stratum, and for every incident upper stratum $S$ the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ restricts to a submersion $S\cap T_R\to R\times(0,\infty)$. On the overlap neighbourhoods where the compositions are defined one requires $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$ and $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$; every compatibility assertion must name the common domain on which the composition is defined. Tubes may be shrunk. For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

(c) **$f$-compatible tubes and controlled lifts.** Let $f:W\to B$ be a stratified submersion onto a smooth manifold. A tube system is **$f$-compatible** if $f\pi_R=f$ on the tubes used. A **controlled lift** of a smooth base field $v$ on $B$ is a field $V$ that is smooth on each stratum and satisfies $df(V)=v\circ f$, $d\pi_R(V)=V|_R\circ\pi_R$ and $d\rho_R(V)=0$ on specified controlled tube neighbourhoods. **Locally bounded** means the ambient norm is bounded on a neighbourhood of every point; this is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of the definition. **Radial controlled lifts** instead satisfy $d\rho_R(V)=\rho_R$ with fixed $\pi_R$ together with the appropriate annular overlap controls.

(d) **Conical product neighbourhoods.** A **conical product neighbourhood along $R$** is a stratum-preserving homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of a point of $R$ to $B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c(L)$ carrying $R$ to the ball times the cone apex, with compact finitely Whitney-stratified $L$. The radial and tangential transports must be compatible with the actual coefficient data when cohomological local systems are deduced; topological existence alone does not supply canonical derived-sheaf transport.

(e) **Finite triangulation of a noncompact space.** In the compactification convention used here, a **finite triangulation** of a noncompact space $X$ consists of finite simplicial complexes $D\subseteq K$ together with a homeomorphism $|K|\setminus|D|\to X$; compatibility with prescribed subsets means they are unions of interiors of retained simplices. This does not assert that algebraic morphisms become simplicial, and real simplicial dimensions do not replace the complex dimensions of the algebraic strata.

derivations.claim: For a smooth stratum $S$ of complex dimension $s$, its algebraic conormal bundle $C_S\subset T^*\mathbb C^N$ has complex dimension $N$: on a Jacobian chart the independent differentials of local equations span the conormal fibres, of rank $N-s$, giving a locally trivial algebraic bundle. On each irreducible component the closure of $C_S$ has dimension $N$ and its boundary has dimension at most $N-1$, since a proper closed subset of an irreducible variety of dimension $N$ has dimension at most $N-1$. Let $D$ be the finite union of these conormal boundaries. If a covector $\lambda$ kills a limiting tangent plane $Q=\lim T_{p_m}S$ at a point outside $S$, then $\lambda$ lies in that boundary: the orthogonal projections of $\lambda$ onto the annihilators of $T_{p_m}S$ are conormal covectors at the points $p_m$ and converge to the projection of $\lambda$ onto $Q^\perp$, which is $\lambda$ because $\lambda$ kills $Q$. Thus every bad limiting-tangent covector lies in the complex algebraic set $D$ of complex dimension at most $N-1$.

Consider the real critical incidence $I_S=\{(a,z):z\in S,\ d(\phi_a|S)_z=0\}$. Differentiation in $a$ surjects onto $T_z^*S$, since every real covector on $T_zS$ extends to one on the ambient Euclidean space; concretely $I_S$ is the real normal bundle via $(z,v)\mapsto(a=z+v,z)$ with $v\perp T_zS$, and the smooth Gram-matrix charts of that normal bundle exhibit it as a smooth real manifold of dimension $2s+(2N-2s)=2N$. In local stratum coordinates its tangent equation is $H_zv+B_z\delta a=0$, where $H_z$ is the Hessian of $\phi_a|S$ and $B_z$ is the surjective parameter derivative. The differential of $(a,z)\mapsto a$ from $I_S$ to $\mathbb C^N$ has kernel $\{(0,v):H_zv=0\}$; since source and target have equal real dimension, it is surjective exactly where $H_z$ is invertible. Hence [F1] makes the parameters with a degenerate stratum critical point null, and a finite union over the strata preserves nullity.

Identify real ambient covectors with complex covectors by $\lambda\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\lambda$. The map $(a,z)\mapsto(z,d\phi_a(z))$ from $\mathbb C^N\times\mathbb C^N$ to the real cotangent bundle is a real smooth diffeomorphism, because $d\phi_a(z)$ is twice the real covector corresponding to $\overline{z-a}$. Therefore the inverse image of each smooth algebraic stratum of $D$ has real dimension at most $2N-2$, and its projection to the $a$-coordinate is a smooth map whose source dimension is smaller than its target dimension $2N$, so every point is critical and [F1] makes the image null; a finite algebraic stratification of $D$ is obtained by successively taking each component's smooth locus and its lower-dimensional singular complement, which terminates because the dimension strictly decreases, and the finite union of the null images is null. Outside this null set, $d\phi_a$ kills no forbidden limiting tangent space.

Finiteness of the critical set uses algebraic geometry rather than a finiteness claim for real analytic sets. Complexify the squared distance to $F_{u,v}(z,w)=\sum_{k=1}^N(z_k-u_k)(w_k-v_k)$ on $S\times\overline S$, where $\overline S$ is obtained by conjugating the equations of $S$. Its complex critical incidence over the parameter space $\mathbb C^N\times\mathbb C^N$ is the algebraic incidence cut out by the two conormal conditions $w-v\perp T_zS$ and $z-u\perp T_w\overline S$; it is isomorphic to the algebraic conormal bundle of $S\times\overline S$, of complex dimension $2N$, equal to the parameter dimension, because the two gradient coefficients $w-v$ and $z-u$ are exactly the conormal vectors that uniquely determine $(u,v)$ for given $(z,w)$. If an irreducible component projects dominantly, [F2] gives a nonempty open of parameters over which its fibres are zero-dimensional and hence finite by [F2]; if not, one avoids its proper closed image closure. The set of real parameters $a$ with $(a,\bar a)$ in this nonempty Zariski open is a nonempty Zariski open of $\mathbb C^N$, hence Euclidean dense: a polynomial vanishing on the real conjugate diagonal vanishes on a real open box after the invertible substitution $(a,\bar a)=(x+iy,x-iy)$, hence is the zero polynomial, so the diagonal meets every nonempty Zariski open. Therefore the prescribed nonempty real open subset meets it in a nonempty real open set, which cannot be contained in the null exceptional sets of steps 1.2 and 2.1; choose such a real parameter $a$. Its real stratum critical points lie in the finite complex fibre over $(a,\bar a)$ just constructed: at $(z,\bar z)$ the real diagonal tangent vectors $(t,\bar t)$ span $T_zS\times T_{\bar z}\overline S$ over $\mathbb C$, and the complex differential of $F$ on them is the real differential of $\phi_a$, so vanishing on the real form implies vanishing on the whole complex tangent.

Choose such an $a$. The Euclidean square distance is bounded below and proper on the closed subset $Z$, and its ambient Levi form is the positive definite Euclidean Hermitian form, so its restriction to every positive-dimensional complex stratum is strongly plurisubharmonic and the sublevel sets exhaust $Z$; on the singular variety the strong plurisubharmonicity statement is the stated inline verification for the concrete function $\|z-a\|^2$, whose ambient complex Hessian is the identity. Steps 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 give exactly the nondegeneracy, limiting-tangent and finiteness conclusions: on a zero-dimensional stratum the Hessian condition is vacuous because its tangent space is zero, and the ambient differential condition there is the step 2.1 exclusion, while the stratum contributes only its finitely many points, and the empty variety has no critical points. The argument works verbatim on any closed affine complex algebraic embedding of $Z$, since only the Euclidean structure of the ambient affine space is used. No stratified product theorem or complex-link identification is used to establish this exhaustion.

Let $f:M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, let $p$ be a nondegenerate critical point of
$f$, and let $\lambda$ be the index of $p$. If $n=\dim M$, then there are local
coordinates $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ centered at $p$ in which

$$f=f(p)-\sum_{i=1}^{\lambda}(x^i)^2+\sum_{i=\lambda+1}^{n}(x^i)^2.$$

finite-dimensional real vector space $T_pM$

If $Q$ is nonzero, let $b>-i$ be its largest nonzero cohomological degree and let $L=\mathcal H^b(Q)|_{W_i}$ be nonzero on a connected component. The finitely many smooth irreducible components of $W_i$ are disjoint and closed in $U_i$; remove the components where $L$ is zero and all but one nonzero component, and choose an affine open $V_0\subset U_i$ in the resulting open, meeting the retained component. Then $V_0\cap W_i$ is smooth affine and $L$ is a nonzero local system on it. Step 1.1 supplies a principal open of it with nonzero $H^i(L)$. Since $W_i\cap V_0$ is closed in the affine $V_0$, the defining function lifts from its coordinate-ring quotient to a function on $V_0$; localizing the latter gives an affine $V\subset U_i$ with $H^i(V\cap W_i,L)\ne0$. The closed embedding $e:V\cap W_i\hookrightarrow V$ has exact pushforward, and $Q|_V=e_*e^*Q|_V$ because all its cohomology is supported there. Thus $H^a(V,\mathcal H^t(Q))=H^a(V\cap W_i,\mathcal H^t(Q)|_{W_i})$. In the bounded spectral sequence $H^a(V\cap W_i,\mathcal H^t(Q)|_{W_i})\Rightarrow H^{a+t}(V,Q)$, [F1] gives $a\le i$ and maximality of $b$ gives $t\le b$. The nonzero term $(i,b)$ has no incoming differential, since those would start at a larger $t$, and no outgoing differential, since those would end at a larger $a$. It is the sole term in its total degree $i+b>0$, contradicting step 1.2. Hence $Q=0$, completing the descending dimension induction and the converse.

Let $P\in{}^pD^{\le0}_c(X)$. For every affine Zariski open $V\subset Y$ its inverse image under the affine morphism $u$ is affine, and derived composition with [F1] gives $H^q(V,Ru_*P)=H^q(u^{-1}V,P)=0$ for $q>0$; the characterization proved in step 2.1 therefore puts $Ru_*P$ in the upper perverse aisle. For $P$ in the lower aisle, apply this to $DP$ and dualize by [F2] to obtain the claimed lower-aisle preservation by $Ru_!$. All zero and empty cases follow from the same zero triangles.

citations.quote: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. For an affine morphism $u:X\to Y$ of complex algebraic varieties and finite-dimensional field coefficients, $Ru_*$ sends ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ and $Ru_!$ sends ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Y)$. More precisely a bounded constructible $K$ belongs to ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ if and only if $H^q(V,K)=0$ for every affine Zariski open $V\subset Y$ and every $q>0$.

Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $P$ be a bounded algebraically constructible complex on a complex variety $Y$ with a finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification. If $a:X\to Y$ is smooth of pure relative complex dimension $d$, then $a^*[d]$ is perverse-exact and $a^!=a^*[2d]$ in complex orientation. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is the restriction of a smooth complex closed embedding of codimension $c$ transverse to every stratum, then $i^*[-c]$ is perverse-exact and $i^!P\cong i^*P[-2c]$. The latter comparison is for complexes constructible for that transverse stratification; no assertion is made for arbitrary closed embeddings.

Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

For the triangulation of [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]], the canonical candidate is $D^{\leq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}$ and $D^{\geq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\}$, using [[prop-cohomology-factors-through-the-derived-category]].

Assume AC. Let $E\to B$ be a numerable complex rank-$n$ bundle over a
paracompact Hausdorff CW complex, with $n\geq1$. Let $P(E)$, $\gamma_E$,
and $x=e((\gamma_E)_{\mathbb R})$ have the conventions of
[[def-complex-projective-bundle-and-tautological-complex-line]].
For each $b\in B$, choose a complex-linear identification $E_b\cong\mathbb C^n$
and denote the resulting fiber inclusion by
$j_b:\mathbb{CP}^{n-1}\to P(E)$.

With the complex orientation on both tautological lines,
$j_b^*x=e(\gamma_{\mathbb R})=:x_{\mathrm{taut}}$. For $n\geq2$ this is a
generator of $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^{n-1};\mathbb Z)$, and
$1,j_b^*x,\ldots,(j_b^*x)^{n-1}$ is an integral cohomology basis. Its
coefficient reductions are a basis over every prime field $\mathbb F_p$.
For $n=1$ the fiber is a point, $j_b^*x=0$, and the basis is $1$.
A comparison with a generator given the opposite normalization introduces
one fixed sign; with the tautological Euler normalization above the sign is
$+1$, independently of $b$ and the chosen complex-linear identification.

Assume AC. For a CW pair $(X,A)$ and local system $\mathcal L$, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients:
$$H^n\bigl(C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;\mathcal L)\bigr)\cong H^n(X,A;\mathcal L).$$
For a connected pair, it is the equivariant-Hom complex on cellular chains after the published right chain action is converted to the left action $g\cdot c=c\cdot g^{-1}$; equivalently its cochains satisfy $\varphi(c\cdot g)=g^{-1}\varphi(c)$. The comparison is natural for cellular maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Let $j:X'\setminus\mathcal X\hookrightarrow X'$ and $u=(f\times1)j$. Over an affine chart of the hyperplane parameter space the complement of the incidence in $\mathbb P^d$ is an affine $d$-space bundle, and $X'\setminus\mathcal X$ is closed in the corresponding bundle over $Y'$; thus $u$ is affine. Apply $R(f\times1)_!$ to the localization triangle $j_!j^*p'^*K[d]\to p'^*K[d]\to i_*i^*p'^*K[d]\to$. By [F1] the first term lies in the perverse lower aisle, so it has no negative perverse cohomology; by proper base change and [F2] the second is $p^*Rf_*K[d]$ and the third is $Rg_*M[1]$. The long exact perverse sequence gives the restriction isomorphisms and the monomorphism. Dualizing the whole construction and using $Di_*=i_!D$, $i^!K'=i^*K'[-2]$ from [F2] gives the Gysin isomorphisms and the epimorphism for $l=1$.

The projective-space cohomology formula gives $Rp_*p^*T=\bigoplus_{a=0}^dT[-2a]$ for every constructible complex $T$, and the identical formula with $d-1$ holds for $p'i:\mathcal X\to X$. To justify the formula as a morphism and not only stalk ranks, cup powers of the tautological Euler class pulled back from $(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ define the map from the direct sum, and on every fibre its map is the usual projective-space cohomology basis, hence an isomorphism by proper base change; the integral power basis is [[lem-complex-tautological-euler-class-restricts-to-the-projective-fiber-generator]], and tensoring the finite cellular cochain complex with $k$ preserves the basis by [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]]. For heart objects $A,B$, adjunction therefore identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(p^*A[d],p^*B[d])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)$: all terms $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[-2a])$ for $a>0$ vanish by [F3].

Write $F=p^*[d]$. For the product projection $p$, the normal slices to $S\times\mathbb P^d$ are precisely the normal slices to $S$. Thus the stalk and costalk boundary conditions characterizing intermediate extension in [F3] are preserved: on a boundary stratum of dimension $s$ their strict bounds $q<-s$ and $q>-s$ become $q<-(s+d)$ and $q>-(s+d)$ after the shift $[d]$. On the dense open, pullback is the shifted pulled-back local system. The no-boundary characterization in [F3] therefore shows that $F$ takes $\operatorname{IC}_S(L)$ to $\operatorname{IC}_{S\times\mathbb P^d}(p^*L)[d]$. Projective space is simply connected by its even-cell CW structure, so projection induces an isomorphism of fundamental groups and $p^*L$ remains irreducible. Hence $F$ is exact, fully faithful by step 1.2, and preserves simples. Every composition factor of $F(A)$ is therefore a pulled-back simple; for a subobject choose a simple subobject, lift its inclusion by full faithfulness, quotient it out and induct on length. This proves the image of $F$ is closed under subobjects and quotients. The derived right adjoint $Rp_*[-d]$ preserves the lower aisle: for $E\in{}^pD^{\ge0}$ and $B\in{}^pD^{\le-1}$, adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(B,Rp_*E[-d])=\operatorname{Hom}(F(B),E)=0$. Thus $Rp_*$ sends ${}^pD^{\ge q}$ into ${}^pD^{\ge q-d}$. Its heart right adjoint is $r={}^pH^{-d}Rp_*$, since the positive-degree truncation of $Rp_*C[-d]$ has no Hom from a heart object. The analogous left adjoint is $\ell={}^pH^dRp_!$, using $p^!=p^*[2d]$. Full faithfulness gives $rF=1$. The kernel of the counit $Fr(C)\to C$ lies in the image of $F$ by subobject closure, and applying the left-exact $r$ shows that kernel is zero, by the adjunction identity $r(\varepsilon_C)=1$. Every subobject $F(B)\hookrightarrow C$ factors through this counit by adjunction. Consequently $Fr(C)$ is exactly the largest subobject coming from $Y$; duality gives the largest quotient $F\ell(C)$.

Put $T=Rf_*K$, $V=R(f\times1)_*p'^*K$ and $U=Rg_*i^*p'^*K$. The graph of $(f,X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d)$ is a closed embedding $a:X\hookrightarrow Y\times\mathbb P^d$ and $f=q a$, where $q$ is the projection. Closed pushforward is perverse-exact directly from the two stratum inequalities in [F3]: on strata inside the image its stalks and costalks are those of $K$, and on the complement they vanish. Applying the lower-aisle calculation of step 2.1 to $q$ therefore gives $T=Rq_*a_*K\in{}^pD^{\ge-d}$. Under the cup-power bases of step 1.2, the map $Rp_*V\to Rp_*U$ is a matrix $(1,\beta):\bigoplus_{a=0}^{d-1}T[-2a]\oplus T[-2d]\to\bigoplus_{a=0}^{d-1}T[-2a]$: restriction carries each of the first $d$ parameter-class powers to the identical power on the incidence bundle, while the last power may be a linear combination involving base classes. Changing coordinates by $(x,z)\mapsto(x+\beta z,z)$ identifies this map with projection. Its discarded summand $T[-2d]$ lies in ${}^pD^{\ge d}$, so the map induces isomorphisms in every perverse degree below $d$, including degrees $-1$ and $0$ for all $d\ge1$. This uses no decomposition of $T$ into its perverse cohomology.

Set $n=d-1$. Step 1.1 gives an isomorphism $L={}^p\tau_{<n}V\simeq{}^p\tau_{<n}U$ and a monomorphism $\iota:{}^pH^nV\hookrightarrow{}^pH^nU$. Apply $Rp_*$ to the two triangles $L\to V\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}V\to$ and $L\to U\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}U\to$. Their five-term exact sequences are ${}^pH^{-1}Rp_*L\to{}^pH^{-1}Rp_*V\to{}^pH^{-1}Rp_*{}^p\tau_{\ge n}V\to{}^pH^0Rp_*L\to{}^pH^0Rp_*V$ and the same sequence for $U$. The first and fourth vertical maps are identities, and the second and fifth are isomorphisms by step 3.1; the five lemma proves that the middle map is an isomorphism. For either $W=V$ or $W=U$, the triangle $({}^pH^nW)[-n]\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}W\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n+1}W\to$ has last term whose $Rp_*$ lies in ${}^pD^{\ge n+1-d}={}^pD^{\ge0}$, by step 2.1. Its perverse cohomology in degrees $-2$ and $-1$ vanishes. The resulting exact sequence gives, naturally in $W$, ${}^pH^{-1}(Rp_*{}^p\tau_{\ge n}W)\simeq{}^pH^{-1-n}(Rp_*{}^pH^nW)=r({}^pH^nW)$, since $-1-n=-d$. Thus $r(\iota)$ is an isomorphism. Proper base change and exact $F$ give ${}^pH^nV=F({}^pH^{-1}T)$, so its right adjoint is ${}^pH^{-1}T$. Adjunction factors $\iota$ as the counit $Fr({}^pH^nU)\to{}^pH^nU$ preceded by the isomorphism $F(r(\iota))$. By step 2.1 its image is exactly the largest pullback subobject of ${}^pH^nU={}^pH^0(Rg_*M)$. Apply this result to $DK$ and dualize using [F2] and [F3]; the middle object is dualized, perverse degrees change sign, and largest subobject becomes largest quotient $F({}^pH^1T)$. This proves every assertion.
